title: going to: Plans and Intentions
grammarTitle: going to — for Plans, Intentions and Predictions
grammarNote: "Going to" используется для выражения ПЛАНОВ и НАМЕРЕНИЙ (то, что уже решено ДО момента речи), а также ПРЕДСКАЗАНИЙ на основе ВИДИМЫХ ПРИЗНАКОВ ("Смотри — он сейчас упадёт!"). Это принципиальное отличие от "will", который используется для спонтанных решений и предсказаний без очевидных признаков.

grammarTable.subject: I
grammarTable.example: I'm going to apply for a master's. (plan, already decided)

grammarTable.subject: He / She / It
grammarTable.example: She's going to work at a startup. (intention)

grammarTable.subject: We / You / They
grammarTable.example: They're going to celebrate on May 30th. (arrangement)

grammarTable.subject: Negative (I)
grammarTable.example: I'm not going to rush — I need time to think.

grammarTable.subject: Negative (She)
grammarTable.example: She isn't going to stay in Kazakhstan for long.

grammarTable.subject: Question
grammarTable.example: Are you going to invite the professor? — Yes, I am.

rows.form: The decision was made BEFORE speaking
rows.example: "I'm going to apply for a scholarship." = She decided this weeks ago.

rows.form: Often used with future time expressions
rows.example: "next year / after graduation / in June / this summer"

rows.form: Often has a specific plan behind it
rows.example: "I'm going to join a startup." = She has already been offered a job.
"I'll help!" (will = deciding NOW) vs "I'm going to help" (already planned).

grammarExtra.title: Use 2: Predictions based on visible evidence

rows.form: You can SEE/KNOW the result is coming
rows.example: "Look at those clouds — it's going to rain!" (I can see the clouds)
"She studied so hard — she's going to pass." (evidence: hard study)
"I think it will rain tomorrow." (general guess, no visible evidence)
"He's going to be late — he missed the bus." (we know this will happen)
"I'm not going to rush into a decision."
"Are they going to celebrate?" — "Yes, they are."

rows.form: Short forms always used in spoken English
rows.example: "I'm going to / She's going to / We're going to"
✅ "I'm going to apply." — Never forget am/is/are!
✅ "She is going to study." — Use base verb after "going to".
✅ "I'm going to go." or "I'll go." — Never use both!
✅ "Look! It's going to rain!" — "going to" for visible evidence.

grammarTip:
"Going to" — три ключевых использования:
① ПЛАН УЖЕ СДЕЛАН: "I'm going to apply for a scholarship." = решила это заранее.
② НАМЕРЕНИЕ: "She's going to help me move." = она собирается, это уже договорено.
③ ПРЕДСКАЗАНИЕ с ОЧЕВИДНЫМИ ПРИЗНАКАМИ: "Look — it's going to rain!" = вижу облака.

💡 Простой тест: "Было ли решение принято ДО этого разговора?" → Да = going to. "Принимаю решение ПРЯМО СЕЙЧАС?" → will.

⚠️ Никогда не говори "I am going to will..." — только одно или другое!

exercises.text: Kamila ___ to Edinburgh next year. She already applied.
exercises.hint: She already decided and applied → "going to" for pre-made plans.

exercises.text: Look at those dark clouds! It ___ (rain).
exercises.hint: Visible evidence (dark clouds) → "going to" for predictions based on what we can see.

opts: She is going to studies abroad.
She is going to study abroad.
She going to will study abroad.
exercises.correct: She is going to study abroad.
exercises.hint: am/is/are + going to + BASE VERB. "She is going to study." ✅

exercises.text: "I'm going to call you later" always means I decided this right now, in this moment.
exercises.hint: "going to" = decided BEFORE the moment of speaking. For decisions made RIGHT NOW, use "will": "I'll call you!"

exercises.text: "___ you going to apply for the scholarship?"
exercises.hint: "going to" question: Are/Is/Am + subject + going to...? → "Are you going to apply?" ✅

exercises.text: I ___ (not / rush) into a decision. I need more time.
exercises.hint: Negative: am/is/are + NOT + going to + base verb. "I'm not going to rush." ✅

exercises.text: Rustam looks at a travel website and says: "I ___ book a ticket to Altai."
exercises.hint: He is looking at the website — he's deciding/intending right now, and it's a clear plan forming → "going to".

exercises.text: Look — she trained every day for a year! She ___ win the competition.
exercises.hint: Visible evidence: she trained very hard → "going to" for predictions based on current evidence.

exercises.text: Zhibek ___ (work) as a research assistant next year.
exercises.hint: She = she (3rd person) → "is going to work". Pre-made plan: she was already offered the position.

exercises.instruction: What does "I was going to call you" mean?
opts: I had a plan to call you (but maybe didn't)
I never wanted to call you
exercises.correct: I had a plan to call you (but maybe didn't)
exercises.hint: "was going to" = past intention that may not have happened. "I was going to call — but I forgot."

exercises.text: "She is going to be late" can be based on evidence (e.g. she missed the bus).
exercises.hint: "going to" for predictions with evidence. "She missed the bus" → clear evidence → "She is going to be late." ✅

exercises.instruction: Choose the correct sentence about a plan.
exercises.text: Amir has been offered a job and has decided to take it. Which sentence is correct?
opts: Amir is going to join the startup.
exercises.correct: Amir is going to join the startup.
exercises.hint: The decision was made before (he was offered + decided) → "going to" for pre-planned intention.

questions.text: "I'm going to apply for a master's." This means:
opts: I decided this before this conversation
questions.correct: I decided this before this conversation
questions.hint: "going to" = pre-made decision, made BEFORE the moment of speaking.

questions.text: "Look at those clouds — it ___ rain." Choose correctly.
questions.hint: Visible evidence (clouds) → "is going to rain". The evidence is right in front of us!

questions.text: "___ she going to stay in Kazakhstan?" — "No, she ___."
questions.hint: Question: Is + she + going to...? Negative short answer: "No, she isn't." (not "she not").

questions.text: "They ___ celebrate on May 30th." Use the correct form.
questions.hint: They = plural → "are going to celebrate". Pre-arranged event.

questions.text: "She is going to studies abroad" is correct.
questions.hint: ✅ "She is going to STUDY abroad." — "going to" is followed by the BASE VERB (no -s, no -ing).

questions.text: Choose the sentence that shows a PLAN (not spontaneous):
opts: "I'm going to move to Almaty in July."
questions.correct: "I'm going to move to Almaty in July."
questions.hint: "I'm going to move..." = specific plan made before. The others use "will" for spontaneous decisions.

questions.text: She ___ (not / join) a big corporation — she prefers a startup.
questions.hint: Negative "going to": isn't/aren't + going to + base verb.

questions.text: "I was going to call you, but I forgot." What does this show?
opts: A past intention that may not have happened
questions.correct: A past intention that may not have happened
questions.hint: "was going to" = a plan that existed in the past. Here: she intended to call but forgot.

questions.text: "He studied every day. He ___ pass the exam." Choose the best form.
questions.hint: "He studied every day" = visible evidence → prediction with "going to". We can see the reason.

questions.text: "___ they going to book the venue?" — "Yes, they ___."
questions.hint: Question: "Are they going to...?" → Short answer: "Yes, they are." (Note: "are", not "going to")

questions.text: "I'm going to be there by 2:30." vs "I'll be there at 2:30." — Difference?
opts: "Going to" is only for the future
questions.hint: Both can express future arrival, but "going to" emphasises a prior decision/arrangement.

questions.text: "She ___ (travel) this summer." — She bought tickets last month. Choose.
questions.hint: She bought tickets = prior arrangement = "going to". The decision and proof exist already.

questions.text: "I am going to will study." is a grammatically correct sentence.
questions.hint: NEVER combine "going to" and "will". Use one or the other: "I'm going to study." OR "I'll study."

questions.text: "___ Zhibek going to send the document tonight?" — "Yes, she ___."
questions.hint: "Is she going to...?" → short answer: "Yes, she is." (subject + is/am/are).

questions.text: "Look at that ice! He ___ (fall)!" Use the correct future form.
questions.hint: Visible evidence (ice + he is slipping) → "going to" for immediate predictions. "He is going to fall!"

questions.text: Which time expression typically goes with "going to"?
questions.hint: "going to" is for FUTURE plans. Time expressions: next week, next year, after graduation, in June, soon.
